findings.code_snippet:
For hooks, sync registers only declared entries on harnesses with verified hook support. Host-local review and approval state remains outside tackroom.

Claude Code plugins (mods, workflows, monitors, output styles, LSP, `bin/`) stay in Claude's native layout under the config root, listed in `<config-root>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. `sync` registers that directory as a marketplace in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`extraKnownMarketplaces`) and enables each relative-path entry (`enabledPlugins`). Claude Code reads it in place: edit, then `/reload-plugins`. User disables (kept across a marketplace rename) and `defaultEnabled: false` are respected; stale enable keys are pruned and removing the marketplace file removes the registration. A name already registered with another source, or a malformed file, is a conflict and nothing is written. `doctor` runs `claude plugin validate` on it when Claude Code is detected.

findings.message: Skill reads from agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). These directories may contain API keys, personal settings, and other credentials that the skill has no legitimate need to access.
findings.remediation: Remove all code or instructions that access agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). If configuration values are needed, pass them explicitly as parameters or environment variables — never read the agent's own config files.

findings.code_snippet:
, targets Codex (`mcp_agents` empty or listing it, `exclude_agents` not listing it), keeps the default `skills/` layout (no `skills:`, `skill_dir:` or `skill_dirs:`) and is not held or blocked. `sync` writes a generated marketplace `tackroom` at `~/.agents/external/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, registers it with `codex plugin marketplace add`, installs with `codex plugin add <name>@tackroom` when the plugin is missing or Codex's copy differs, and removes `*@tackroom` plugins that are no longer declared with `codex plugin remove`. Codex then loads that source's skills and MCP servers from the plugin alone, so tackroom links no skills and writes no `[mcp_servers]` rows for it. `enabled = false` under `[plugins."<name>@tackroom"]` in `~/.codex/config.toml` is respected and shown as `plugins off`. `status`, `sync --dry-run` and `doctor` never run `codex`. Tested with codex-cli 0.159.2.

`sync --pull` runs `git pull --ff-only` in the private canonical repository before reconciliation.

findings.code_snippet:
`sync` repairs drift to the pin; `skill update` explicitly advances it. `doctor` audits external source content and fails on materialization drift.

Add a source without editing YAML: `tackroom skill sources add mattpocock/skills --skills tdd,grill-me` (or `--all`; without either, an attended run lists the skills to pick and an unattended one fails with the list). It pins the newest commit at least 3 days old (`--latest` pins the head), writes the entry with `materialize: true`, refuses to overwrite a different `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (an identical copy, as `npx skills add` leaves it, is adopted), then syncs. `tackroom skill sources` lists configured sources and the ones installed outside tackroom (Claude Code plugins, `npx skills`); `search` queries skills.sh. A source that Claude Code already has as a plugin gets `exclude_agents: [claude]`, so Claude does not load its skills twice. Two repos with the same basename need a distinct `name:`; `add` picks `<owner>-<repo>` itself.

findings.message: Skill establishes unauthorized persistence across sessions via cron jobs, startup scripts, or state files. Session persistence allows an attacker to maintain access beyond the current interaction.
findings.remediation: Remove any persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, startup scripts, state files). Skills should not maintain state across sessions without explicit user consent.

findings.message: npx commands without a version suffix (e.g. @1.0.0) create a rug-pull risk if the upstream server is compromised and publishes a malicious update.
